jurisdiction.name: Argentina
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Argentina has no AI-specific national law as of October 2026; some 25 comprehensive AI bills are pending, one with a committee report (November 2025), and data-protection reform bills have repeatedly lapsed. Ley 25.326 on personal data bars judicial or administrative decisions about people based solely on automated profiling, and Argentina has approved Convention 108 (Ley 27.483) and its 2018 amending protocol (Ley 27.699), which adds the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions. At national level the Jefatura de Gabinete's interministerial AI roundtable and its 2023 recommendations for reliable AI, SIGEN's 2026 AI controls guide (mandatory for the national public sector), and AI programmes of the justice and security ministries and the federal prosecution service set the rules for government use; the data protection agency AAIP runs an AI transparency programme and issued an AI guide, and the central bank's technology-risk rules cover AI models. Provinces are active: Santa Fe's 2025 constitution gives a right to human intervention in AI decisions, Buenos Aires province has risk-based AI rules and a 2026 AI framework decree, Buenos Aires City has an AI strategic plan and facial-recognition rules, and many provincial courts have AI acordadas; Rosario, Córdoba, Mendoza and Salta have municipal AI ordinances.
lead_institutions: Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros (Secretaría de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología)
Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública
Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires
Gobierno de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 11 October 2026, covering national laws, decrees and bills, the national government and ministries, regulators, Buenos Aires City and the provinces of Buenos Aires, Córdoba, Santa Fe, Neuquén, San Luis, Río Negro, Salta and Mendoza, and the cities of Rosario, Córdoba, Mendoza, Salta and Mar del Plata. Searches were made in Spanish and English. The provinces of Tucumán, Entre Ríos, Chubut and Misiones were not reached, and Mendoza province was only partly covered; they are listed as pending. Some official websites could not be read automatically, including the Senate's bill pages and parts of Buenos Aires City's official bulletin. Bills, including the national AI and data-protection bills, are listed as pending rather than as instruments. Pending: a national AI law, data-protection reform, the 2019 national AI plan (no official copy online), Santa Fe's law on AI in administrative procedure, and the Buenos Aires Supreme Court's draft AI regulation.

instruments.english_title: Administrative Decision 750/2023 creating the Interministerial Roundtable on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG); Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina

instruments.summary: Creates the Mesa Interministerial sobre Inteligencia Artificial within the Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros as a cross-cutting forum on the advance and application of AI across the economy and society, within an ethical, sustainable-development and digital-transformation framework, with the purpose of designing an integral AI strategy to be applied by the national executive. As amended by Decisión Administrativa 899/2024, it is chaired by the Secretaría de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología and co-coordinated with the Secretaría de Asuntos Estratégicos, and its members are the Jefatura de Gabinete and the ministries of Defence, Economy, Foreign Affairs, Health, Security, Human Capital, Justice and Deregulation; the coordinators may invite other public or private bodies.

instruments.publisher_name: Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública

instruments.official_title: Ley 25.326 de Protección de los Datos Personales
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Act (Law 25,326)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Nación Argentina (sanctioned 4 October 2000); partially promulgated by Decreto 995/2000
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force. Consolidated text on InfoLEG/argentina.gob.ar shows the last amendment by Ley 26.343 (B.O. 9 January 2008). The control body is the Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública (Decreto 1558/2001 art. 29 as substituted by Decreto 899/2017). Article 20 has not been regulated. Replacement bills (executive bill 0012-PE-2023 and later proyectos) have not been enacted. The text contains no AI-specific provision.
instruments.scope: Public and private files, registers and databases of personal data in Argentina
instruments.summary: Argentina's general data protection law, protecting personal data held in public and private files, registers and databases and creating the habeas data action. It sets lawfulness, consent, data quality, security and cross-border transfer rules that govern the use of personal data to train and run AI systems. Article 20 provides that judicial decisions and administrative acts that assess human conduct may not be based solely on the result of computerised processing of personal data that defines the profile or personality of the person concerned, and that such acts are incurably void.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law governing AI processing of personal data; art. 20 bars judicial and administrative decisions on human conduct based solely on automated profiling.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 1558/2001 - Protección de Datos Personales - Reglamentación de la Ley N° 25.326
instruments.english_title: Decree 1558/2001 regulating the Personal Data Protection Act
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force. Amended by Decreto 1160/2010 (B.O. 13 August 2010) and Decreto 899/2017 (B.O. 6 November 2017), which made the Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública the control body of Ley 25.326. The regulation of article 20 (decisions based on computerised processing) reads 'Sin reglamentar'.
instruments.scope: Data controllers and users of personal data subject to Ley 25.326
instruments.summary: Regulatory decree implementing Ley 25.326, approving in its Annex I the article-by-article regulation of the data protection law and setting a 180-day deadline for existing databases to register and comply. It details consent, data quality, access and rectification rights, registration of databases, sanctions and the control body, now the Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública. Article 20 of the law, on decisions based solely on computerised processing of personal data, is left unregulated.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Implementing rules of the data protection law that governs AI processing of personal data; confirms that the automated-decision clause (art. 20) has no regulation.

instruments.official_title: Ley 27.699 - Apruébase el Protocolo Modificatorio del Convenio para la Protección de las Personas con Respecto al Tratamiento Automatizado de Datos de Carácter Personal
instruments.english_title: Law 27,699 approving the Protocol amending the Convention for the Protection of Individuals with regard to Automatic Processing of Personal Data (Convention 108+)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Nación Argentina
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: Approval law sanctioned 9 November 2022 and published in the Boletín Oficial on 30 November 2022 (No. 35058). The law only approves the Protocol (CETS 223, Strasbourg, 10 October 2018); the date of deposit of Argentina's instrument of ratification and the Protocol's entry into force were not verified on an Argentine official source. The approval of the original Convention 108 and its Additional Protocol is a separate law, Ley 27.483 (B.O. 2 January 2019).
instruments.scope: Argentina as a party to Council of Europe Convention 108 as amended
instruments.summary: Law by which Congress approves the Protocol amending Council of Europe Convention 108 (Convention 108+), signed in Strasbourg on 10 October 2018, whose Spanish translation is annexed. The approved text gives every person the right not to be subject to a decision significantly affecting them based solely on automated processing without their views being taken into account, and the right to obtain knowledge of the reasoning underlying data processing whose results are applied to them. It also adds data breach notification and other modernised obligations for controllers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National approval of Convention 108+, which includes a right against solely automated decisions and a right to the reasoning behind automated processing.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 70/2023 (DNU) - Bases para la Reconstrucción de la Economía Argentina
instruments.english_title: Necessity and Urgency Decree 70/2023: Bases for the Reconstruction of the Argentine Economy (AI-piloted aircraft clause)
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación, in general agreement of ministers)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: Necessity and urgency decree (DNU) dated 20 December 2023, published 21 December 2023 (B.O. No. 35326); it contains no specific commencement clause. Article 203 substituted article 79 of the Código Aeronáutico (Ley 17.285); the consolidated Código Aeronáutico on argentina.gob.ar shows art. 79 in the text given by art. 203 of Decreto 70/2023. The AI-piloted aircraft regulation the article calls for was not found.
instruments.scope: Civil aviation under the Código Aeronáutico (Ley 17.285)
instruments.summary: Omnibus necessity and urgency decree deregulating large parts of the Argentine economy, including amendments to the Código Aeronáutico (Ley 17.285). Its article 203 rewrites article 79 of the Code so that every crewed aircraft must carry a qualified pilot-in-command, the remote pilot is the commander of an uncrewed aircraft, and 'aircraft piloted by artificial intelligence shall be subject to special regulation'. This is the only explicit AI provision in the decree.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Inserts into the Aeronautical Code an explicit legal mandate for special regulation of AI-piloted aircraft.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 98/2023 - Reglamentación de la Ley N° 27.553
instruments.english_title: Decree 98/2023 regulating Law 27,553 on electronic or digital prescriptions and telehealth
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force; amended by Decreto 345/2024 (B.O. 22 April 2024), which did not change the AI clause (Annex art. 4, item k, unchanged in the consolidated text). The Ministerio de Salud is the enforcement authority (art. 2).
instruments.scope: Platforms that issue, validate or dispense electronic or digital prescriptions or manage telehealth services
instruments.summary: Decree approving the regulation of Ley 27.553 on electronic and digital prescriptions and telehealth, naming the Ministerio de Salud as enforcement authority and creating the Licencia Sanitaria Federal. Annex article 4 sets duties for prescription and telehealth platforms on data processing, security and confidentiality. Item k provides that any use of artificial intelligence must observe the restrictions imposed on it, may only support professional decision-making, and always requires supervision by health professionals.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rule limiting AI in telehealth and e-prescription platforms to decision support under professional supervision.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 159/2023 - Plataforma Digital del Sector Público Nacional. Decreto N° 87/2017. Modificación
instruments.english_title: Decree 159/2023 amending Decree 87/2017 to add the 'TINA' AI chatbot to the National Public Sector Digital Platform
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: Published in the Boletín Oficial on 22 March 2023 (No. 35135). No modifying norms are listed on InfoLEG. Whether the TINA chatbot is still operated was not checked.
instruments.scope: Agencies and jurisdictions of the National Public Sector covered by Decreto 87/2017; provinces, CABA and municipalities invited to adhere
instruments.summary: Decree adding the State chatbot 'TINA' to the National Public Sector Digital Platform and making it the official conversational channel of the national State. Its recitals describe TINA, set up under Resolución 14/2022 of the Secretaría de Innovación Pública, as an AI tool that automates tasks through natural-language conversation. Article 2 lists its minimum functions, including information on procedures, online transactions linked to Mi Argentina, proactive messages and referral to human operators for matters needing a person; provinces, CABA and municipalities are invited to adhere.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Decree establishing an AI chatbot as an official national government service channel, including referral to human operators.

instruments.official_title: Ley 27.506 - Régimen de Promoción de la Economía del Conocimiento
instruments.english_title: Law 27,506: Knowledge Economy Promotion Regime
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Nación Argentina
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force; substantially amended by Ley 27.570 (B.O. 26 October 2020) and Decreto 679/2022 (B.O. 11 October 2022). Under art. 20 as substituted by Ley 27.570 the regime runs until 31 December 2029. The AI reference in art. 2(i) is unchanged in the consolidated text.
instruments.scope: Companies carrying out promoted knowledge-economy activities that register in the Registro Nacional de Beneficiarios
instruments.summary: Law creating a promotion regime with tax and contribution benefits for knowledge-economy companies such as software, audiovisual production, biotechnology and professional services. Article 2(i) lists among the promoted activities the manufacture, set-up, maintenance and introduction of goods and services for production automation characterised by industry 4.0 technologies 'such as artificial intelligence, robotics and industrial internet'. Beneficiaries must register and meet employment, export or R&D requirements.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding incentive law naming AI-based automation as an eligible promoted activity.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 749/2024 - Apruébase Reglamentación del Título VII - Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (RIGI) - Ley Nº 27.742
instruments.english_title: Decree 749/2024 regulating the Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI) of Law 27,742
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force; amended several times, most recently by Decreto 748/2026 (B.O. 18 August 2026) and Decreto 868/2026 (B.O. 4 September 2026) per the consolidated-text notes. The technology-sector definition naming AI was restated by art. 2 of Decreto 105/2026 (B.O. 19 February 2026), which also extended the RIGI adhesion deadline by one year. A separate 'Super RIGI' bill for new industries including AI (0005-PE-2026) passed the Cámara de Diputados on 24 June 2026 and is pending in the Senado.
instruments.scope: Investors in large projects adhering to the RIGI under Title VII of Ley 27.742
instruments.summary: Decree approving the regulation of the Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI) created by Title VII of Ley 27.742 (Ley Bases), which grants tax, customs and foreign-exchange benefits and regulatory stability to large investment projects. Annex article 3 defines the eligible sectors; the technology sector covers innovative production of goods and services in fields including biotechnology, the software industry, robotics and artificial intelligence. It sets the procedures and evaluation of adhesion applications.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding investment-incentive regulation that names AI as an eligible technology sector.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 111/2024 - Programa Nacional Integral de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia - Créase
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Justice Resolution 111/2024 creating the Comprehensive National Programme on Artificial Intelligence in Justice
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio de Justicia
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 9 April 2024 (RESOL-2024-111-APN-MJ) and published in the Boletín Oficial on 11 April 2024; art. 8 was replaced by Resolution MJ 116/2024 (B.O. 11 April 2024), and art. 1 was replaced and art. 7 repealed by Resolution MJ 149/2024 (B.O. 7 May 2024). Resolution MJ 469/2026 (September 2026) refers to it as in force.
instruments.scope: Ministerio de Justicia; AI projects in the Ministry and the justice system
instruments.summary: Creates the Programa Nacional Integral de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia to promote the use of AI to improve administrative procedures and judicial processes, ensuring respect for fundamental rights, and citing Disposición 2/2023 and the UNESCO AI ethics recommendation. The programme is run by a coordinator with an ad honorem advisory committee chaired by the Minister, and must present an annual plan covering prior impact assessments and audits before any AI deployment in the Ministry or the justice system, AI projects, AI risk control, training on AI ethics for the Ministry and the national judiciary, and stakeholder meetings.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ministry-level AI governance programme for the justice sector, with impact-assessment and risk-control planning duties.
instruments.evidence_reference: arg-deep-review-R2-2026-10-11. Status note: Res. MJ 116/2024 replaced art. 8 to order publication; Res. MJ 149/2024 placed the programme under the Dirección Nacional del Sistema Argentino de Información Jurídica (Secretaría de Justicia). Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Boletín Oficial gazette entry: 'Fecha de publicación 11/04/2024' and notice footer 'e. 11/04/2024 N° 20091/24'; signed 'Ciudad de Buenos Aires, 09/04/2024'.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 469/2026 - Mesa Estratégica de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia (MEIAJ) - Creación
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Justice Resolution 469/2026 creating the Strategic Roundtable on Artificial Intelligence in Justice
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio de Justicia
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 21 September 2026 (RESOL-2026-469-APN-MJ) and published in the Boletín Oficial on 23 September 2026. The MEIAJ must submit a preliminary Estrategia de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia within 90 days of its first meeting (art. 10); no strategy had been published by 11 October 2026.
instruments.scope: Ministerio de Justicia units; invited representatives of the judiciary, public prosecutors, provinces, universities and others
instruments.summary: Creates the Mesa Estratégica de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia (MEIAJ) in the Ministry of Justice's Unidad Gabinete de Asesores to help draft an AI Strategy for the Justice system, following technical assistance from the EU's EL PACCTO 2.0 programme and the French École nationale de la magistrature. Its functions include mapping existing AI initiatives, identifying priorities, proposing principles, pilot use cases, training and indicators, and submitting a preliminary strategy within 90 days of its first meeting. Article 7 states the strategy is a planning and coordination instrument, not a general AI regulatory regime, and must respect data protection, information security, intellectual property and transparency rules and promote human oversight, traceability and risk assessment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sets up the body that will draft a justice-sector AI strategy and fixes its guiding safeguards.
instruments.evidence_reference: arg-deep-review-R2-2026-10-11. Status note: Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Boletín Oficial gazette entry: 'Fecha de publicación 23/09/2026' and notice footer 'e. 23/09/2026 N° 69016/26'; signed 'Ciudad de Buenos Aires, 21/09/2026'.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 710/2024 - Unidad de Inteligencia Artificial Aplicada a la Seguridad (UIAAS) - Creación
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Security Resolution 710/2024 creating the Artificial Intelligence Unit Applied to Security
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio de Seguridad
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 26 July 2024 (RESOL-2024-710-APN-MSG) and published in the Boletín Oficial on 29 July 2024. No amendment or repeal found in the Boletín Oficial to October 2026.
instruments.scope: Ministerio de Seguridad and the federal police and security forces
instruments.summary: Creates the Unidad de Inteligencia Artificial Aplicada a la Seguridad (UIAAS) in the Ministry of Security's Dirección de Ciberdelito y Asuntos Cibernéticos, headed by that director and staffed by representatives of the federal police and security forces, with the mission of preventing, detecting, investigating and prosecuting crime using AI. Its listed functions include patrolling open social networks, apps and the dark web, real-time analysis of security-camera images with facial recognition, machine-learning analysis of historical crime data to predict future crimes, cyber-threat detection, drone surveillance, and detection of suspicious financial transactions. The unit must adapt its functions to the cyber-patrolling guidelines of Resolución 428/2024.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ministry-level instrument authorising police use of AI, including facial recognition and predictive policing.
instruments.evidence_reference: arg-deep-review-R2-2026-10-11. Status note: Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Boletín Oficial gazette entry: 'Fecha de publicación 29/07/2024' and notice footer 'e. 29/07/2024 N° 48636/24'; signed 'Ciudad de Buenos Aires, 26/07/2024'.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 428/2024 - Pautas, principios, criterios, recomendaciones y directivas para las labores preventivas de los delitos que se desarrollan en ambientes cibernéticos
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Security Resolution 428/2024 on guidelines for preventive police work on crimes in cyberspace (open-source cyber-patrolling)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio de Seguridad
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 27 May 2024 (RESOL-2024-428-APN-MSG) and published in the Boletín Oficial on 28 May 2024; it is cited as in force by Resolution MSG 710/2024. No amendment or repeal found in the Boletín Oficial to October 2026.
instruments.scope: Federal police and security forces
instruments.summary: Sets the rules federal police and security forces must follow when carrying out preventive work on crimes in cyberspace, limited to publicly accessible websites and open digital sources, with data-protection limits under Ley 25.326, a ban on processing sensitive data and minors' posts without judicial authorisation, and the deletion of data when no case is opened. Article 5 provides that the use of software or tools for automated information processing based on artificial intelligence, machine learning, expert systems, neural networks, deep learning or future techniques must be limited to the strict needs of the regulated activity and supervised by the Ministry of Security.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rule on police use of AI tools in open-source online surveillance (art. 5).
instruments.evidence_reference: arg-deep-review-R2-2026-10-11. Status note: Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Boletín Oficial gazette entry: 'Fecha de publicación 28/05/2024' and notice footer 'e. 28/05/2024 N° 33171/24'; signed 'Ciudad de Buenos Aires, 27/05/2024'.

instruments.english_title: SIGEN Resolution 197/2026 approving the Artificial Intelligence Controls Guide
instruments.issuing_authority: Sindicatura General de la Nación
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina; Sindicatura General de la Nación
instruments.current_status: Signed 16 June 2026 (RESOL-2026-197-APN-SIGEN) and published in the Boletín Oficial on 22 June 2026. instruments.scope: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires
instruments.summary: Requires all areas and agencies of the Government of the Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires to promote and ensure the implementation of AI solutions in government management and in interaction with residents, to improve efficiency, service quality and productivity. It makes AI a priority for procedures on business-activity authorisations, building permits and notices, infraction records and all citizen-service channels, and empowers the Secretaría de Innovación y Transformación Digital (Jefatura de Gabinete) to implement AI in other procedures and to issue complementary and operational rules.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: City-level executive decree mandating AI adoption across the CABA administration and designating the authority that issues the City's AI governance rules.

Art. 2 requires the City executive's areas and agencies to observe the plan's guidelines in every project involving AI systems, under Decreto 97/26. The City's AI plan web page describes the plan as covering 2025-2027.
instruments.scope: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires
instruments.summary: Approves the City government's AI Strategic Plan, which sets a vision, guiding principles (people-centred public value, human oversight and institutional accountability, proportional transparency and explainability, privacy, equity, security, sustainability), a risk-based approach and four axes: governance, adoption and engagement (including mandatory training of City staff); research, development and innovation; production and implementation of AI; and economic development and the AI ecosystem. It foresees an AI Board as an advisory council and an AI unit in the City observatory, and is to be implemented through action, tactical and operational plans; City executive agencies must observe its guidelines in all AI projects.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Provincial-level (CABA) AI strategy for the City government, binding on executive agencies as guidelines for AI projects.

instruments.official_title: Resolución N.º 98/SECITD/26 - Lineamientos Operativos para la Gobernanza y Uso Responsable de Sistemas y Agentes de Inteligencia Artificial en el ámbito del Poder Ejecutivo de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires

instruments.scope: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires
instruments.summary: Approves operational guidelines that City executive agencies must observe in every project to develop, acquire, contract, configure, pilot, deploy, use or scale AI, and creates an Internal Inventory of AI Initiatives within the Secretaría de Innovación y Transformación Digital. The guidelines prohibit entering sensitive personal data, confidential City information or credentials into open or non-institutional generative-AI platforms, treat AI outputs as inputs requiring human review, require visible disclosure when AI interacts with residents or produces public communications (with human-review and complaint channels for higher-impact uses), set rules for deploying AI agents, and require a documented pre-deployment assessment, proportional monitoring and contractual clauses on data use and no unauthorised training.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mandatory AI governance rules for the CABA executive, covering generative AI, AI agents, disclosure, risk assessment, an AI inventory and procurement clauses.

It takes a human-centred approach (AI as a tool that never substitutes human capacities), sets guiding principles such as equity and digital inclusion, data protection and privacy, transparency and explainability, teacher supervision, sustainability and pedagogical relevance, and defines governance structures at strategic, technical-operational and school levels.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sector (education ministry) AI governance framework for the CABA school system.

instruments.scope: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires
instruments.summary: Approves a guide of recommendations and guidelines for responsible and sustainable use of AI and generative-AI agents in the City's judiciary (excluding the Tribunal Superior and Ministerio Público, per the related MIA pilot). instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Judicial-branch AI guidance for the CABA courts, covering generative AI and human oversight of AI outputs.

instruments.summary: Approves guidelines for all staff of the Buenos Aires provincial administration, whatever their employment modality, who use generative-AI systems. They require express authorisation by the immediate superior before using generative AI, human control before and after use with no delegation of decisions to AI outputs, ethical use, transparency about AI-generated content, confidentiality and data protection (it is strictly forbidden to input information that may compromise security), information security, evaluation of results and awareness training, and prohibit personal use and inappropriate or manipulated content.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Generative-AI use guidelines for all staff of the Buenos Aires provincial administration, requiring prior authorisation and human control.

instruments.official_title: Resolución N° 9/2025 de la Subsecretaría de Gobierno Digital - Reglas para el desarrollo, implementación y uso responsable de sistemas de Inteligencia Artificial (IA) para la Administración Pública de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
instruments.english_title: Resolution 9/2025 of the Digital Government Undersecretariat: Rules for the development, implementation and responsible use of AI systems in the Public Administration of the Province of Buenos Aires

instruments.publisher_name: Gobierno de la Provincia de Buenos Aires

instruments.scope: Buenos Aires
instruments.summary: Sets rules, mandatory for every provincial agency that develops, researches, contracts or uses any AI system, to protect fundamental rights. It requires a documented preliminary risk classification (unacceptable risk - prohibited, e.g. subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities and social scoring; high risk - e.g. biometric identification, critical infrastructure, education, justice, democratic processes and labour relations; limited; and minimal), a mandatory algorithmic impact assessment for high-risk systems, lifecycle risk management, data governance, bias mitigation, consent for personal data in training, prior notice when residents interact with AI, and registration of AI systems in a Registro de Inteligencia Artificial; the Dirección Provincial de Innovación Digital is the enforcement authority.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Risk-based binding AI rules for a provincial administration, including prohibitions, impact assessment, disclosure and an AI register.

instruments.publisher_name: Gobierno de la Provincia de Buenos Aires

instruments.scope: Buenos Aires
instruments.summary: Approves the provincial AI framework as the governing instrument for developing, implementing and using AI in the Buenos Aires provincial public sector, with eleven guiding principles (including human centrality, transparency and explainability, human oversight and no automated decisions that adversely affect fundamental rights, non-discrimination, technological sovereignty and no vendor lock-in). Provincial agencies must obtain the prior intervention of the Subsecretaría de Gobierno Digital before any development, use, contracting or renewal of AI systems and before substantial changes; the Subsecretaría (enforcement authority) sets standards, promotes risk and impact assessment, homologates AI solutions and is to promote a manual for AI procurement. The decree creates a Registro de Inteligencia Artificial in which agencies must register their AI systems, invites municipalities to adhere, and keeps Resolutions 4/25 and 9/25 for matters it does not cover.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Governor's decree establishing the overarching AI governance framework, prior-approval regime and AI register for the Province of Buenos Aires.

instruments.official_title: Resolución SC 1719/26 - Proyecto de Reglamento para el desarrollo y uso responsable de la Inteligencia Artificial de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de la provincia de Buenos Aires

instruments.publisher_name: Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
instruments.current_status: Resolution registered as RSC-1719-2026 on 19 June 2026 (expte. 3000-21862-2026). instruments.summary: Publishes for consultation a draft AI regulation that would bind judges, officials and staff of the provincial judiciary, court auxiliaries and contracted AI providers across the AI lifecycle, and creates a Comisión de Gobernanza y Uso de Inteligencia Artificial (Planning, IT and Jurisdictional Services secretariats) as enforcement authority. Meanwhile the resolution itself states that judicial staff remain fully responsible for acts in which AI intervened and must exercise substantive, documented control of outputs, that AI may never be delegated decisions resolving a case, the weighing of evidence or the legal reasoning of a judgment, and that personal-data processing with AI must comply with Ley 25.326.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Draft binding AI regulation for the largest provincial judiciary in Argentina, with interim non-delegation rules already set by the Court.

instruments.summary: Approves the Ministerio Público's framework for responsible use of generative AI and makes 'ChatIA', its in-house generative-AI system, the only authorised platform for staff interaction with foundation models. Every staff member must sign a sworn declaration of knowledge of and compliance with the framework before access; breaches are disciplinary offences, and all ChatIA activity may be audited. The annex prohibits delegating decisions to AI, personal use, using third-party credentials and entering protected information, and requires validation of every output and reporting of biased or discriminatory results.

instruments.scope: Santa Fe
instruments.summary: The new provincial constitution applies all rights in digital environments and commits the Province to ethical, secure, human-centred technology development (art. 28). instruments.summary: Protocol, mandatory for all members of the Neuquén judiciary, on using generative-AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and DeepSeek. It requires users to avoid entering personal or sensitive data of parties, to verify, review and validate all outputs (chatbots are not search engines and may be biased or inaccurate), and to inform recipients when a ruling or judicial document was prepared with AI, with the signatory responsible for the content. Official AI accounts may be assigned only to staff who prove training and obtain express authorisation from the judiciary's IT commission, and each AI tool incorporated into the judiciary's systems must be approved by the Court with its scope and limits explained.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mandatory generative-AI rules, including AI-use disclosure in judicial decisions, for the Neuquén provincial judiciary.

instruments.issuing_authority: Superior Tribunal de Justicia de la Provincia de San Luis

instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Superior Tribunal de Justicia on 21 August 2024 (expte. ADM 15367/24); point IV orders publication on the judiciary's website and for one day in the provincial Boletín Oficial y Judicial (gazette date not checked).
instruments.scope: San Luis
instruments.summary: Approves a four-phase programme (assessment and planning, training, pilot, full deployment) to introduce the generative-AI tool Iurix Mind and other generative-AI tools in the San Luis judiciary, coordinated by the Secretaría de Informática Judicial, and creates a monitoring committee (Court ministers, IT secretariat and the vendor) to set phase dates and evaluate efficiency, user satisfaction, data protection and confidentiality. It states that AI does not relieve judges and officials of their constitutional and legal duties: judicial decisions and final responsibility rest exclusively with them, AI is a support tool that does not replace legal analysis, and they must keep up to date on the tools' functioning and limitations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Provincial supreme-court instrument governing the adoption of generative AI in the San Luis judiciary, with human-responsibility rules.

instruments.scope: Río Negro
instruments.summary: Approves a good-practice protocol for generative-AI use by judges, officials and employees of the Río Negro judiciary. Personal use of generative AI for official duties requires authorisation by the Judicial IT Committee chair after review by the Systems Directorate (with an application form and register), projects using generative AI in court work need prior approval by the Court, and mandatory training is to be organised. The protocol sets objectives on responsible use, prohibits delegating decision-making to AI, requires protection of personal and confidential data, and covers transparency, explainability and risks such as hallucinations and bias.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Early provincial judicial generative-AI protocol in Argentina, cited as a model by other courts.

instruments.scope: Salta
instruments.summary: Approves a protocol, mandatory for staff of the centralised and decentralised Salta executive, governing the request, design, deployment, supervision, registration, monitoring and discontinuation of public AI agents and generative-AI tools (high-risk institutional AI is left to specific frameworks). Agencies must file a reasoned request to the Secretaría de Modernización y Servicios Públicos defining need, scope, risks, data sources and supervisors; agents may only perform specific, bounded tasks, with general-purpose, unrestricted-autonomy or decision-substituting agents excluded; and a mandatory internal Registro Provincial de Agentes Públicos de Inteligencia Artificial is created for traceability and evaluation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding provincial rules on AI agents and generative AI in the Salta administration, with an agent register.

No usage-limit interruption; the three earlier records were re-checked and fixed (i-338245c4109a now points to Disposición 2/2023 itself, the 'Ley simple' page being only an explainer). Download limits (BACKFILL step 4) applied: curl --max-time 60, gazette searches instead of bulk downloads. Pres. 206/CMCABA/25 judiciary AI guide); the records for the legal acts were kept and the duplicate document records dropped.
